data.name: Asghar
data.gender_notes: Asghar is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Asghar is an Arabic name meaning 'younger' or 'smaller'. It is often used to differentiate between elders and juniors, and carries the connotation of humility and tenderness. In Islamic history, it is famously associated with Ali Asghar, the infant son of Imam Hussain (RA). The name Asghar carries the meaning “Younger, Humble, Small in Age” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in English, Urdu, Arabic. Parents who choose Asghar usually hope their child will grow to embody younger, humble, small in age and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of innocence, humility, and sacrifice — especially in relation to the Karbala legacy.
data.etymology: Asghar belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Younger, Humble, Small in Age.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Asghar total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_arabic.name: أَسْغَر
in_arabic.long_meaning: الصغیر، الأصغر، الأقل: مصدر صغَرتَ، صَغَرَ، صِغَراً، صِغَرتُم، صَغَرتم، صَغَروا، صِغَروا. يُشير هذا الاسم إلى الشخص الأصغر سنًا، أو الأقل من حيث الكمية أو الجودة. في القرآن الكريم، يظهر هذا الاسم في سورة القصص، آية 87، حيث يعود إلى إبراهيم عليه السلام ويقول: "يا عجلان، أَبِي رَأَيْتَ أَنِ ائْتُكَ بِكَذِبٍ عَلى بَيِّنَةٍ فَتَأْمَنَنَّهُ، وَتَكُن مِنَ الْغَالِبِينَ". وفي الحديث النبوي الشريف، يقول الرسول عليه السلام: "الرجل يُسمَّى الصَغيرُ أَنَّهُ صغيرُ سِنًّا، وَصغيرُ مَالٍ، وَصغيرُ شَأنٍ".

in_urdu.name: اسغَر
in_urdu.long_meaning: اسغَر کا مطلب چھوٹا، کم، صغیر ہوتا ہے۔ یہ نام کسی کے لیے چاہیے جس کا جنم کم عمر میں ہوا ہو یا وہ کم عمر میں انتقال کرنے لگے۔ اس نام کی ابتدائی اور اسلامی اصطلاحات میں بھی اس کا ذکر ملتا ہے۔

in_hindi.name: अस्गर
in_hindi.long_meaning: अस्गर का अर्थ है छोटा, कम, सघर। यह नाम उन लोगों के लिए उपयुक्त है जिनका जन्म कम उम्र में हुआ है या जिन्होंने कम उम्र में ही अपनी जिंदगी को समाप्त कर लिया।

in_pashto.name: اسغَر
in_pashto.long_meaning: اسغَر دا لومړی معنا چټک، کم ښوديړ دی. دغه نوم د هغوی لپاره چاېیې چې ځټک عمر کې زېږۍږي یا د هغوی په عمر کې د ژوند ګټیږي.

in_english.name: Asghar
in_english.long_meaning: Asghar is an Arabic name meaning younger, smallest, or lesser. This name is often associated with individuals born in a younger age or those who have passed away in a younger age. In Islamic tradition, the name Asghar is also mentioned in the Quran and Hadith.

celebrity_usage: Ali Asghar ibn Hussain (infant martyr of Karbala)
data.cultural_impact: The name Asghar holds great cultural significance in Islamic communities, especially within the Shia sect. It is commonly used as a hypocorism for Ali Asghar, the second and youngest son of Imam Hussain (AS), an eventual Grandson of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH). Imam Hussain is regarded as an inspiring and revolutionary figure for his unyielding resistance against tyrants. Often remembered and celebrated for his unique bond with his children, especially Imam Hussain's youngest son Ali Asghar. This name holds cultural importance due to the memorable narrations of Ali Asghar’s ultimate sacrifice representing love, devotion and loyalty towards his father and the Prophet’s Household (Ahlul-Bayt).
data.spiritual_significance: Possessing the meaning of 'younger,' 'smaller' or 'tender,' Asghar also represents spiritual significances beyond a literal age reference. Within the Islamic context, it also signifies humility, vulnerability and purity. It's an evocative reminder of the childlike innate virtues that every believer strives to maintain, such as meekness, surrender, and unwavering faith. The spiritual significance of the name Asghar is also seen through the lens of Ali Asghar, who despite his tender age, embodied the determination and unyielding spirit of his father, Imam Hussain (AS), through his ultimate sacrifice. Ultimately, the name Asghar signifies the importance of being humble, vulnerable, and faithful in the face of adversity, following the footsteps of the Prophet's household. (Sources: Seerat e Hussain/ The Life of Imam Hussain, Shia and Sunni Hadith)
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Asghar in Islamic tradition symbolizes nearness to Allah. It is derived from the Arabic word "asghar," meaning "the younger one" or "the closest one." This name is often given to a child who is considered close to Allah, reminding the child to strive for a deep connection with the divine.

islamic_reference.note: Traditional Islamic name with deep spiritual significance in Islamic culture

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Asghar was a Persian prince in the 7th century. The name Asghar carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Asghar was a Persian prince during the Sassanid Empire. He is known for his bravery and loyalty to his father, Chosroes II.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Asghar remains relevant in modern Muslim society, representing a bridge between traditional Islamic values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Islamic names.

name_in_real_life.story: Khalid Asghar, a teacher in Cairo, Egypt, shares that their name Asghar meaning "Younger, Humble, Small in Age" has been a source of inspiration throughout their life, motivating them to be a positive influence in their community.
